newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian parliament to vote on new government.
newsitem.headline: Romanian parliament to vote on new government.

text.p: The cabinet of Romania's new centrist government formed after last month's elections was expected to win parliamentary approval on Wednesday together with the coalition's reformist programme.
The vote of confidence in Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea's team and the government's economic policies was due to be taken by secret ballot, a parliamentary official said.

President Emil Constantinescu named Ciorbea last month after his centrist Democratic Convention (CDR) won the November 3 parliamentary elections, ousting the leftist Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) to form a cabinet with the Social Democratic Union (USD) and the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR).

Ciorbea will present parliament with his government's programme intended to tackle what his coalition sees as hardships caused by stalled reorms and poor economic planning during the PDSR's four years in power.
The programme includes steps to boost economic reforms, control the budget deficit, fight poverty and unemployment and stimulate foreign investments.

Romania's macro-economic stabilisation, the resumption of talks with the International Monetary Fund on blocked credits as well as the country's proposed integration into the European Union and NATO are also main features of the programme.

Both the new coalition and its economic programmes are expected to be approved by parliament on the strength of an accord signed last week by the CDR, USD and the UDMR pledging support for the new cabinet.
The three political groups hold a majority of 287 of parliament's 486 seats.

Ciorbea entrusted key ministerial jobs in the proposed cabinet to representatives of the main National Peasant Party, the backbone of the CDR bloc, and to the former ministers of reform, justice and transport who served in the cabinet led by ex-prime minister and USD leader Petre Roman.
Roman, Romania's first post-communist prime minister, was ousted in 1991 by rioting miners who opposed his reforms.
The new cabinet also includes representatives of the UDMR, a party standing for the interests of 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians -- a first in Romania's post-Communist history.
